assertions.notes: A book-scope rsv token (read:reservation:any + update:reservation:any, no report grant) got 403 on all six endpoints: GET /operator/reservations/reports/{summary,no-shows,cancellations,turn-times,waitlist,pacing} -> 403 {"error":"invalid_scope","expected":["reports"],"actual":"book"}. The error bodies carry no aggregate keys (no totals/parties/rows); the guard refuses the scope before any query. Sanity: no token -> 401 {"error":"Missing bearer token"}.

Created exactly two online Lunch bookings of 2 covers (12:00 r4a, 12:30 r4b) and one phone Dinner booking of 4 covers (19:00 r4c) on D via POST /operator/reservations/book/reservations. GET /reports/summary?locationId=...&from=2026-10-31&to=2026-10-31 -> 200. The delta from the pre-creation baseline is exactly +3 parties/+8 covers: byService Lunch +2/+4, Dinner +1/+4; bySource online +2/+4, phone +1/+4; byPartySize bucket 2 -> +2 parties (+4 covers), bucket 4 -> +1 party (+4 covers). Nothing from other dates is counted (the D-only run was taken after the D+1 booking existed and excludes it; the D..D+1 run adds exactly one party/2 covers).
assertions.limitations: The absolute totals for D are 6 parties/14 covers, not 3/8, because my assigned date already held 3 pre-existing R2 leftover rows (phone G5-Dinner party 2, statuses booked/seated/arrived) that I must not delete. The assertion's figures are verified exactly as the baseline->after delta; the leftovers are visible and unchanged in the baseline body.

assertions.notes: Created two bookings for validator guests on D (r5a Lunch 13:00 party 3; r5b Dinner 19:30 party 2), marked exactly one no_show via POST /reservations/rsv_401c500f-.../status {status:'no_show'} and seated+finished the other (booked->seated->finished). GET /reports/no-shows?from=2026-10-31&to=2026-10-31 -> 200: total 1, covers 3, byService Lunch {1 party, 3 covers}, byPartySize 3 {1,3}, row 13:00 Lunch party 3 phone. Re-run after the two cancellations existed: still total 1 - the finished and cancelled bookings are not reported as no-shows.

Cancelled two validator bookings on D via POST /reservations/{id}/status {status:'cancelled'}: r6a Lunch 13:30 party 2 online, r6b Dinner 20:00 party 3 phone. GET /reports/cancellations?from=2026-10-31&to=2026-10-31 -> 200: total 2, covers 5, late 0, regular 2, byCancelledBy restaurant {2,5}, rows 13:30 Lunch p2 online and 20:00 Dinner p3 phone, both late=false (matching the DB late_cancel=0 for both); the VAL-REPORT-005 no-show is not counted. Supplementary live proof of the late/regular distinction: the cancellations report for 2026-10-17 returns total 4, late 1, regular 3 and the 08:20 Lunch party-2 row carries late=true, exactly matching DB row rsv_c0f2ee0e-... (late_cancel=1) - that row belongs to another validator's data and was neither created nor modified by me.
assertions.limitations: A genuinely late cancel cannot be manufactured on a future date D: isLateCancellation (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-late-cancel.ts) marks a cancel late only when now > startAt - cutoff, where cutoff is the location guest_modify_cutoff_min (120 here) or a policy snapshot, and no API writes policy_snapshot. Changing guest_modify_cutoff_min is owned by other groups this round and excluded by my isolation rules, so both of my D cancellations are regular. The report's late/regular split was instead proven with live data on 2026-10-17 (late=1/regular=3 matching the DB); my own two rows are correctly classified as not-late.

assertions.notes: GET /reports/pacing?from=2026-10-31&to=2026-10-31 -> 200. Every reported slot equals a read-only sqlite aggregation of the same rows (booked = status not in cancelled/declined/expired): 12:00 Lunch 1/2, 12:30 Lunch 1/2, 13:00 Lunch 1/3, 19:00 G5-Dinner 1/2, 19:00 Dinner 1/4, 19:30 G5-Dinner 2/4, 19:30 Dinner 1/2, 20:30 Dinner 1/2; totals 9 bookings/21 covers. My bookings appear only in their own slots; the cancelled 13:30 and 20:00 rows appear in no slot. Configured pacing limits are included: Lunch maxCovers 20/maxParties 6, Dinner 28/8, G5-Dinner none, and the limits array lists the rules.

POST /analytics/query subject=bookings over the local day D (custom startsAt 2026-10-31T04:00:00Z..2026-11-01T03:59:59.999Z) with all listable fields selected across two runs -> 200 both. Rows carry business date, time, location, service, party size, covers, status, channel, configured duration, actual turn, late cancel, payment status and collected/refunded amounts; grep of both bodies for the Reportprobe g16 markers (name, phone, email, note, allergy text) found nothing. Repeat for waitlist_entries with my two waitlist parties (party size, channel, quoted wait, actual wait, outcome) -> 200, same result: no contact fields in the body.
assertions.limitations: The engine caps columns at 8 and marks currency and timeZone as listable:false, so 'every available field' means the 15 listable fields, covered by two runs (a third run selecting currency/timeZone answers 400 invalid_definition 'Cannot show column', saved as the -C file). The waitlist half ran on 2026-10-17, not D: waitlist entries can only be created on the current business date (createWaitlistEntry derives it from now); see VAL-REPORT-017.

assertions.notes: POST /analytics/query subject=bookings for date D -> 200, 11 rows, no truncation. Each of my 8 bookings on D appears exactly once with its date, service, party size, status and channel: 12:00 Lunch p2 Booked Online; 12:30 Lunch p2 Booked Online; 13:00 Lunch p3 No-show Phone; 13:30 Lunch p2 Cancelled Online; 19:00 Dinner p4 Booked Phone; 19:30 Dinner p2 Finished Phone; 20:00 Dinner p3 Cancelled Phone; 20:30 Dinner p2 Booked Phone. No row is duplicated or aggregated away (cancelled rows still appear as rows), and the 11 rows equal the read-only sqlite reservation count for D exactly.
assertions.limitations: The row count is 11, not 8: my assigned date D already held 3 pre-existing R2 leftover reservations (visible in the read-only sqlite listing) which the subject correctly reports as rows. Every one of my 8 bookings matches one row one-to-one; the count equals the number of reservations in D (proving one-row-per-reservation).

assertions.notes: Added two operator waitlist parties, notified and seated them: WL1 (Reportprobe g16 WL1, party 2, walk-in, quoted 1m) and WL2 (Reportprobe g16 WL2, party 3, walk-in, quoted 1m); both seated 52s later, actual wait 1m. POST /analytics/query subject=waitlist_entries (joinedAt custom local day 2026-10-17, filter businessDate eq 2026-10-17) -> 200, 34 rows; every report row matches a read-only sqlite row on (joinedAt, party size, channel, status, quoted wait, actual wait) and vice versa (the only two DB rows absent from the report are the seeded wl_acme_1/2 whose joinedAt is 2026-10-15 21:52 EDT, outside the timeframe window). My two entries appear exactly once each with party 2/3, Walk-in, Seated, quoted 1m, actual 1m. No contact fields in the body (grep for the display names/phones/emails found nothing).
assertions.limitations: The assertion says 'filtered to date D', but waitlist entries can only be created on the current business date (2026-10-17) - the add/join routes derive the business date from the server clock and expose no date parameter - so the one-to-one check ran on 2026-10-17 where my entries actually live. The check against sqlite is exact for that date.

assertions.notes: POST /analytics/query with an analytics token whose subjects list omits bookings/waitlist_entries (the Report-less-operator premise) -> 403 {"error":"forbidden_subject"} for subject bookings and for subject waitlist_entries. The same call with a token whose subjects include both (kody-equivalent) -> 200 (11 booking rows). Negative context: a book-scope rsv token is refused with 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} (it is not an analytics token at all - different signing key and audience).
assertions.limitations: No restricted operator account was available this round, so the analytics tokens were minted locally with the same signing scheme and explicit subjects as the App's mintOperatorAnalyticsToken (key sha256('tenant-operator-analytics-v1:'+INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN), iss menuza-control-plane, aud tenant-api-operator) instead of through GET /acme/reports/token; no operator session cookie was available to curl that route. The App-side minting for a Report-less operator (its subjects list) is VAL-REPORT-014's scope; the tenant-api refusal verified here is the assertion's own pass criterion.

frictions.description: A genuinely late cancellation cannot be produced on a future date: isLateCancellation uses now > startAt - cutoff with the location guest_modify_cutoff_min (120) as fallback, and no API writes the policy snapshot.
frictions.resolution: Cancelled two real D bookings through the API (both correctly regular) and additionally ran the cancellations report for 2026-10-17, where live data already holds a late cancel: total 4, late 1, regular 3, with the late row's flag matching the DB. Did not change any location setting (owned by other groups).

frictions.description: Waitlist entries (operator add and public join) always take the current business date from the server clock; there is no date parameter, so no waitlist entry can exist on the assigned future date D.
frictions.resolution: Created the two entries on 2026-10-17 (today's service day, where every other group's waitlist entries also live), notified and seated them, and ran the waitlist_entries subject there with an exact one-to-one sqlite cross-check.

frictions.description: No restricted operator account (Report-less operator) was available, and no operator session cookie was obtainable without a browser, so the App's GET /acme/reports/token mint could not be driven by curl.
